disease_mechanism_summary: Rett syndrome is caused by de novo loss-of-function variants in X-linked MECP2 (EVIDENCE, Monarch MONDO:0010726; PMID 40673967). Affected girls are somatic mosaics for MeCP2 function because of random X-inactivation. Loss of this methyl-DNA reader/NCoR-recruiting protein produces broad, individually small transcriptional dysregulation plus chromatin changes (H3K9/H4K16 hyperacetylation, directly observed and pharmacologically reversible in patient fibroblasts; EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749), with arrested neuronal maturation and reduced neurotrophic tone rather than neurodegeneration (EVIDENCE, PMID 40673967). Two facts dominate design. First, the phenotype reflects ongoing absence of MeCP2 function and is reversible after symptom onset: peripheral TAT-MeCP2 extended Mecp2-/y lifespan >50% with CA2 soma rescue (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749), and ASO normalisation of MeCP2 reversed adult phenotypes in the reciprocal duplication model (EVIDENCE, PMID 26605526). Second, MECP2 is dose-toxic upward (duplication syndrome), so any MeCP2-adding or upregulating therapy must be dose-capped, and in a mosaic female a non-selective agent loads wild-type-expressing neurons as readily as null ones (EVIDENCE, PMID 26605526). The residual uncertainty is not what starts the disease but which downstream node to drug and within what window; a further caution is that behavioural rescue in Mecp2+/- mice can occur while prefrontal/anterior cingulate projection abnormalities persist (EVIDENCE contradictory, PMID 40673967), so rodent behavioural endpoints can overstate benefit. Decision support only, not medical advice.
leverage_points: Ongoing-dependency biology: because MeCP2 absence rather than fixed damage drives the phenotype, post-onset molecular correction remains competent (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749; PMID 26605526). The strongest asset of the whole programme.
Endogenous-locus routes are intrinsically closer to dose-capped than cDNA/mRNA/protein addition, because native promoter regulation sets the per-cell level (INFERENCE, PMID 26605526; PMID 29282321).

A human-cell on-target pharmacodynamic readout already exists: H3K9/H4K16 hyperacetylation reversal in patient fibroblasts (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749) - modality-agnostic, cheap, usable for dose/activity calibration.

Downstream trophic pharmacology is clinically derisked: trofinetide is approved for Rett on the IGF-1 axis (EVIDENCE, NCT04776746), proving a non-MECP2 node can clear a regulatory bar - and simultaneously raising the bar for any successor.

Brainstem nTS synaptic hyperexcitability is a concrete, measurable, drug-reversible lesion in Mecp2 mice (EVIDENCE, PMID 25147297) - the only mechanistic link retrieved from MeCP2 loss to the dominant morbidity driver.
Small molecules distribute irrespective of X-inactivation status, bypassing the mosaic corrected-cell-fraction threshold that bounds every cell-fraction-limited modality (INFERENCE, PMID 26605526).

reviews.why_it_could_work: Acting on the endogenous silenced wild-type MECP2 allele is the only route that supplies real MeCP2 under native regulation, the correct structural answer to bidirectional dose sensitivity (INFERENCE, PMID 26605526; PMID 29282321). Xist ASO plus DNA-methylation inhibition achieved large MECP2 up-regulation from the inactive X in cells, and brain-specific genetic Xist ablation plus 5-aza-dC reproduced selective Xi reactivation in vivo (EVIDENCE, PMID 29282321). The CNS route is mature: nusinersen and tofersen establish chronic intrathecal dosing, and MECP2-lowering ASOs already engaged this axis in adult brain with functional benefit (EVIDENCE, PMID 26605526).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: All-or-nothing dilution. Xi reactivation is a per-cell binary switch, so partial knockdown in many cells is useless, unlike a conventional lowering ASO where partial effects are partially beneficial. Intrathecal exposure is steeply surface-weighted, so the plausible outcome is reactivation in a superficial cortical subset with little in deep structures or brainstem respiratory nuclei - biomarker-positive, clinically inert. Dose escalation then collides not with MECP2 overdose but with chromosome-wide X-linked gene overdose, since Xist knockdown is not gene-selective (INFERENCE, PMID 29282321). The only in vivo proof used genetic Xist ablation plus a systemic DNMT inhibitor, not an ASO-only regimen (EVIDENCE contradictory, PMID 29282321), and no clinical-stage oligonucleotide exists for Rett (EVIDENCE, ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-05).
reviews.rationale: The proposed experiment is correctly built to kill the approach cheaply: it measures per-cell conversion in allele-distinguishable Mecp2+/- females with an ASO-alone arm, scores co-reactivated X-linked genes in the same cells as a paired safety readout, maps cortex vs hippocampus vs brainstem, and pre-specifies conversion rather than behaviour as primary - the right choice given PMID 40673967. INVESTIGATE not PURSUE because the drug-like version of the mechanism has never been demonstrated; the agent's THERAPEUTIC HYPOTHESIS NOT TESTABLE YET is nearly right, but the gating experiment is cheap and uses an existing model, so the correct action is to run it rather than shelve the idea. The splice-switching sub-route is a separate, far more conventional decision and should be assessed on stratum size first (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

reviews.why_it_could_work: The only modality with direct pharmacological proof: intraperitoneal TAT-MeCP2 extended Mecp2-/y lifespan >50% with CA2 soma-size rescue, and TAT-MeCP2e2 reversed H3K9/H4K16 hyperacetylation in patient fibroblasts (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749). A protein with finite half-life is withdrawable and titratable, a genuine advantage over gene addition for a bidirectionally dose-sensitive gene (INFERENCE, PMID 26605526; PMID 35460749).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Non-selective cell-penetrating uptake into a mosaic tissue collapses the therapeutic window: the dose that loads null neurons also loads co-resident wild-type-expressing neurons, which must not be loaded (EVIDENCE, PMID 26605526). MeCP2 is an entirely nuclear chromosomal methyl-CpG-binding protein with no extracellular site of action (EVIDENCE, UniProt P51608), so BBB, plasma membrane and nuclear import are three serial barriers for a 486-aa cargo, and the fraction of neurons achieving nuclear occupancy was never established as a delivery parameter. Mouse brain is ~1/1000 human volume and the mortality-driving brainstem nuclei were never characterised. Chronic lifelong dosing of a viral-TAT-fused nuclear antigen carries high anti-drug-antibody risk (INFERENCE). No MeCP2 protein therapeutic has reached the clinic despite mouse data since 2022 (EVIDENCE, ClinicalTrials.gov Rett search).
reviews.rationale: The experiment is the best available and well judged: it abandons the null male (which structurally cannot reveal overdose, having no wild-type cells), uses allele-distinguishable Mecp2+/- females, measures per-cell nuclear occupancy - never previously reported - as two superimposed dose-response curves, includes brainstem, and excludes survival and behaviour. A null closes the route on mechanism rather than after years of protein engineering. The verdict stays LOW PRIORITY rather than INVESTIGATE because the dominant failure mode is not merely untested but structurally adverse: non-selectivity is a property of cell-penetrating peptides, not a parameter to optimise, and even a positive window leaves BBB shuttle engineering, human-scale biodistribution and chronic immunogenicity unsolved. The agent's NO PLAUSIBLE DELIVERY PATH is defensible; fund the window-mapping study only as a small decisive add-on where a group already doses this tool compound, not as a standalone programme.

reviews.why_it_could_work: The replacement logic is biologically correct - supplying MeCP2 activity rescues null cells (EVIDENCE, PMID 35460749) - and the post-onset window stays open, so a non-integrating repeat-dosed supply is not disqualified by timing (EVIDENCE, PMID 26605526). A trimmed construct with destabilising UTRs/degrons might in principle cap per-cell output (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Pharmacological mismatch compounded by absent delivery. mRNA produces a transient, per-cell-uncontrolled protein burst into a gene that is toxic upward (EVIDENCE, PMID 26605526) - the worst available match for a bidirectionally dose-sensitive chromatin reader. Uptake is blind to X-inactivation status, so wild-type-expressing neurons receive the same cargo. Intrathecal/ICV LNP gives patchy, largely ependymal, perivascular and glial transfection with weak deep-parenchymal neuronal uptake, and no carrier achieves near-pan-neuronal mRNA delivery across a human-sized brain (INFERENCE). No MECP2 mRNA/LNP work was retrievable and no RNA therapeutic appears in the Rett landscape (EVIDENCE, PubMed zero hits; ClinicalTrials.gov Rett search), so a programme begins with carrier invention, not optimisation. Model fitness is inadequate by the agent's own assessment.
reviews.rationale: I agree with the agent's NO PLAUSIBLE DELIVERY PATH and with its framing: the gating question is carrier existence, generic to CNS mRNA delivery, and should not be charged to a Rett budget. REJECT applies to the MECP2 mRNA programme, not to the cheap iPSC arm testing whether per-cell MeCP2 output can be capped at all by construct design - that answers a MECP2-specific question for little money and a negative kills the idea permanently. Rejecting now does not foreclose revisiting if the field independently solves deep CNS neuronal mRNA delivery; it declines to fund carrier invention from a rare-disease budget when two endogenous-locus routes exist that are intrinsically closer to dose-capped.

reviews.why_it_could_work: Mechanistically the best-matched biologic in the dossier: Trk receptors are on the neuronal surface, so no nuclear entry is needed and the MECP2 dose ceiling is bypassed entirely (INFERENCE, UniProt P51608). Intranasal painless NGF mutein improved survival and behaviour in already-symptomatic MeCP2+/- females - the correct mosaic genotype, dosed post-onset (EVIDENCE, PMID 37633263). Pathology is arrested maturation without degeneration, so a trophic stimulus acts on structurally correctable neurons (EVIDENCE, PMID 40673967). Clinical precedent exists: rhIGF-1 completed Phase 2 and trofinetide is approved (EVIDENCE, NCT01777542; NCT04776746).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: A real but shallow symptomatic effect in the wrong anatomy. Intranasal exposure declines steeply rostro-caudally; whether brainstem respiratory and autonomic nuclei see Trk-activating concentrations in a human-sized brain (nose-to-brainstem ~1-2 cm in mouse vs ~10 cm in human) is unmeasured, and uniformity was not quantified in the source (INFERENCE, PMID 37633263). The convergence premise is asserted, not demonstrated, and sits awkwardly with the broad small-magnitude transcriptional phenotype (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied). The clinical bar is now incremental benefit over approved trofinetide on the same axis (INFERENCE, NCT04776746), and chronic Trk agonism carries epileptogenic (TrkB/BDNF in a seizure-prone brain) and nociceptive (residual TrkA/p75) risk (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
reviews.rationale: The experiment is well chosen and cheap: region-resolved mutein concentration plus pTrkA/pTrkB/pAKT/pERK with an inhibitor epistasis arm and paired plethysmography, in an existing model, with a pre-specified brainstem-to-olfactory-bulb ratio as primary. It tests target engagement rather than a composite behavioural endpoint known to dissociate from circuit correction (PMID 40673967). LOW PRIORITY rather than INVESTIGATE for comparative reasons: the small-molecule route to the same node already has demonstrated brainstem target engagement in Mecp2 tissue (PMID 25147297), systemic dosing, and far simpler chronic-dosing economics, so the protein format should be funded only if the small-molecule branch fails its pharmacological validation or if the biodistribution study shows the nasal route uniquely reaches brainstem. Positive brainstem engagement with an apnoea fall would move this to INVESTIGATE immediately.

reviews.why_it_could_work: The best-connected mechanism in the dossier. BDNF is reduced in human Rett autopsy brain and in Mecp2-deficient mouse brain, so the node is deficient in humans and not only in mice (EVIDENCE, PMID 37986936). LM22A-4 rescued deficient TrkB phosphorylation and improved respiratory function in heterozygous females (EVIDENCE, PMID 22302819), normalised nTS synaptic hyperexcitability and acutely reversed spontaneous apnoeas (EVIDENCE, PMID 25147297), and increased CA1 spine density as much as recombinant BDNF with the effect abolished by K-252a and ANA-12 and absent in wild-type slices - consistent with partial agonism acting only where BDNF tone is low (EVIDENCE, PMID 37986936). Small molecules reach null and wild-type cells alike, so mosaicism is not a delivery barrier and the MECP2 dose ceiling is irrelevant (INFERENCE, PMID 26605526). Trofinetide's approval proves the axis can clear a regulatory bar (EVIDENCE, NCT04776746), and ketamine is a repurposable clinical probe (EVIDENCE, PMID 40612906; NCT02562820 terminated for funding, not futility).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Chasing a pharmacologically invalid target. Whether LM22A-4 and 7,8-DHF genuinely activate TrkB at brain-achievable exposures is unresolved - the agent flagged a wider-literature challenge it could not retrieve or verify (INFERENCE, contradictory, unverified) - and pleiotropy is independently indicated by 7,8-DHF effects in placenta and cardiomyocyte mitochondria (INFERENCE, PMID 36764626; PMID 28677406). If the mouse rescues are off-target, SAR would track an unknown mediator and the programme cannot be optimised. Secondary failure mode is translational: the realistic bar is incremental benefit over approved trofinetide on a composite behavioural endpoint of the kind shown to move without circuit normalisation (EVIDENCE, PMID 40673967), and the retrieved LM22A-4 effects are acute and partly symptomatic with no chronic disease-modification data in mosaic females (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, PMID 22302819; PMID 25147297).
reviews.rationale: This is the highest-value experiment in the dossier and is correctly specified: blinded quantitative pTrkB concentration-response against a recombinant BDNF reference, abolition in TrkB-knockdown neurons, ANA-12/K-252a epistasis, free brain concentration versus EC50 at the efficacious dose, and chemoproteomics if phenotype survives TrkB loss. It is cheap, fast, needs no new model, and a negative saves a multi-year chemistry programme while possibly identifying a better target. The agent's MECHANISM UNCERTAIN is exactly right and is why this is INVESTIGATE rather than PURSUE: the rescue data are strong and in the right genotype and right anatomy, but the drug mechanism is unverified, and a good-sounding mechanism must not outrank an unresolved target-validity question. Running ketamine in parallel as the cheapest clinical probe of the same branch is sensible since apnoea and arousal readouts move within days.

reviews.why_it_could_work: It targets the dominant morbidity driver with an objective, titratable endpoint, and delivery is genuinely favourable: the brainstem is well perfused, small-molecule CNS drugs reach it, mosaicism is irrelevant and the MECP2 dose ceiling does not apply (EVIDENCE/INFERENCE, PMID 25147297; PMID 26605526). The lesion is concrete and drug-reversible: MeCP2 loss causes nTS synaptic hyperexcitability reversed by BDNF in slices and by a peripherally dosed small molecule in vivo with acute apnoea reversal (EVIDENCE, PMID 25147297), present and improvable in heterozygous females (EVIDENCE, PMID 22302819). Sponsors and regulators have shown willingness to run respiratory-endpoint trials in Rett (EVIDENCE, NCT02790034; NCT07503444).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Repeating sarizotan. The only direct clinical test of this hypothesis failed: sarizotan was developed specifically for Rett respiratory symptoms and terminated without efficacy on primary or secondary variables (EVIDENCE contradictory, NCT02790034). The model therefore has a documented false-positive history - mouse apnoea counts supported a mechanism that failed in humans. Apnoea in Mecp2 mutants is partly arousal-state dependent, so unstratified counts can reflect activity rather than rhythmogenesis (INFERENCE contradictory, PMID 25147297). The failure mode is endpoint and engagement failure rather than absence of a candidate molecule, and no systemic neuromodulator can be confined to respiratory nuclei, raising sedation, seizure-threshold and cardiovascular liabilities in a population with high baseline seizure burden. Any success is symptomatic, not disease-modifying (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
reviews.rationale: The experiment does something rare and valuable: it treats the measurement instrument as the object of study. Arm A quantifies within-animal test-retest variance of state-stratified versus total apnoea rate - i.e. whether any feasible trial could detect a plausible effect - and Arm B anchors every behavioural result to terminal nTS electrophysiology, with sarizotan as a built-in benchmark of the human-negative node. This genuinely discriminates the three competing explanations for the sarizotan failure (wrong node, no engagement, endpoint failure), which no new molecule should be advanced without. The agent's INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE is fair, but the gating work is cheap and its most decision-relevant output - a qualified, state-resolved endpoint - is reusable by every future respiratory programme in Rett regardless of molecule, so INVESTIGATE is warranted. The branch overlaps heavily with the small-molecule trophic approach via LM22A-4 and should be resourced as one engagement-anchored package, not twice.

comparative_judgment:
Nothing here earns PURSUE, and that is the honest read. The disease has outstanding causal genetics and a rare gift - demonstrated post-onset reversibility (PMID 35460749; PMID 26605526) - but every approach's dominant failure mode is currently untested, and in three cases that failure mode is delivery or target validity rather than biology.

Across modalities for the same hypothesis (MeCP2 restoration), the ordering is driven entirely by dose control and cell access, not by mechanism, because the mechanism is identical. Oligonucleotide (Xi reactivation) ranks highest because it alone acts on the endogenous locus under native regulation, the correct structural answer to bidirectional dose sensitivity (PMID 26605526; PMID 29282321) - but it trades the MECP2 overdose problem for a chromosome-wide X-linked overdose problem and depends on a per-cell binary switch never achieved with an ASO alone in vivo. Protein ranks below it because its non-selectivity is structural, not a tunable parameter: in a mosaic brain the dose that corrects null neurons overloads the wild-type-expressing half, and MeCP2's purely nuclear site of action (UniProt P51608) imposes three serial barriers. Tellingly, the headline efficacy result came from a null male - the one genotype that by construction cannot reveal the dominant risk. mRNA ranks last and is rejected: it adds an uncontrolled per-cell burst on top of the same non-selectivity and the same undelivered anatomy, with zero retrievable preclinical work for this target. The general lesson is that for a bidirectionally dose-sensitive gene, endogenous-locus modalities dominate addition modalities, and dose capping should be achieved genetically rather than pharmacokinetically.

For the trophic hypothesis, small molecule clearly dominates protein: it has demonstrated brainstem target engagement in Mecp2 tissue (PMID 25147297) where the protein's brainstem exposure is unmeasured, it is systemically dosed, it is chronically dosable in children, and apparent partial agonism confined to low-BDNF-tone cells (no effect in wild-type slices, PMID 37986936) is exactly the self-limiting property this disease needs. The protein's one advantage - a surface receptor target, no nuclear entry - is shared by the small molecule, so there is little reason to prefer the harder format.

The two highest-value next steps are not the most biologically exciting. They are the TrkB target-deconvolution package and the brainstem endpoint-qualification study, because both are cheap, both can kill multi-year commitments early, and both produce reusable assets (a validated pTrkB dose-selection biomarker; a variance-characterised, state-resolved apnoea endpoint). They are substantially the same experiment viewed from two ends and should be funded as one package built around LM22A-4. Both trophic and brainstem approaches also face a comparator problem that pure biology hides: trofinetide is already approved on this axis (NCT04776746), so any successor must differentiate - and respiratory/autonomic morbidity, which trofinetide has not been shown to address, is the natural place to do it.

What would change my mind. Moving the Xi-reactivation ASO to PURSUE requires ASO-alone conversion of a substantial fraction of null neurons in vivo, with measurable brainstem conversion, reactivation confined to few X-linked loci and no dependence on a DNMT inhibitor. Reviving MeCP2 protein requires a genuinely cell-selective delivery concept, not dose optimisation; separable per-cell occupancy curves in mosaic females would reopen it as a delivery-engineering problem with a defined target product profile. Moving the TrkB small molecule to PURSUE requires reproducible, TrkB-dependent, ANA-12-shiftable pTrkB activation with free brain exposure above EC50, after which the pivotal study should be built on brainstem apnoea rather than a behavioural composite. Reviving MECP2 mRNA requires the field - not this programme - to solve deep CNS neuronal mRNA delivery. Conversely, I would downgrade the entire brainstem branch if state stratification fails to reduce apnoea variance, because then no respiratory trial is interpretable regardless of molecule.
what_is_known: EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID 35460749): Peripheral TAT-MeCP2 reached brain, extended Mecp2-/y lifespan >50% and rescued hippocampal CA2 neuron size - direct pharmacological proof that supplying MeCP2 activity is therapeutic.
EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID 35460749): TAT-MeCP2e2 reversed H3K9/H4K16 hyperacetylation in patient fibroblasts - an existing human-cell on-target pharmacodynamic assay usable by any modality.

EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID 26605526): ASO-mediated normalisation of MeCP2 reversed phenotypes in adult symptomatic MECP2 duplication mice, establishing adult reversibility and that ASOs can tune MeCP2 in mature brain.
EVIDENCE (contradictory, PMID 26605526): MECP2 overexpression causes duplication syndrome - the upper dose bound is real and bounds every addition or upregulation strategy.

EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID 29282321): Xist ASO plus a DNA-methylation inhibitor achieved ~30,000-fold MECP2 up-regulation from the inactive X in cells; the in vivo synergy required genetic Xist ablation plus 5-aza-dC, i.e. not an ASO-only drug regimen.

EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID 25147297): MeCP2 loss causes synaptic hyperexcitability in nTS respiratory neurons, reversed by BDNF in slices and by a systemically dosed small molecule in vivo with acute reversal of spontaneous apnoeas.

EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID 22302819; PMID 37986936): LM22A-4 rescued TrkB phosphorylation and respiratory function in heterozygous Mecp2 females and increased CA1 spine density as much as BDNF, blocked by K-252a/ANA-12 and absent in wild-type slices; BDNF is reduced in human Rett autopsy brain.

EVIDENCE (contradictory, NCT02790034): Sarizotan, developed specifically for Rett respiratory symptoms, was terminated for lack of efficacy on primary and secondary endpoints - a failed approach that must shape any new respiratory programme.

EVIDENCE (supportive, NCT04776746; NCT01777542): Trofinetide is approved for Rett and rhIGF-1 completed Phase 2 - the trophic axis is clinically validated and is also the comparator any successor must beat.
EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID 37633263): Intranasal painless NGF mutein improved survival and behaviour in already-symptomatic MeCP2+/- females - correct mosaic genotype, post-onset dosing.

EVIDENCE (contradictory, PMID 40673967): Environmental enrichment normalised rotarod and open-field performance in Mecp2+/- mice while prefrontal/anterior cingulate projection abnormalities persisted - rodent behavioural endpoints are dissociable from circuit correction and must not be primary.

EVIDENCE (inconclusive, NCT02562820; PMID 40612906): The one Rett ketamine trial was terminated for funding withdrawal rather than futility, leaving an approved, CNS-penetrant, BDNF/TrkB-linked probe available and unexhausted.

EVIDENCE (contradictory, ClinicalTrials.gov Rett searches 2026-10-05; PubMed zero hits): No oligonucleotide, no MeCP2 protein and no RNA therapeutic appears at any clinical stage in Rett; the clinical landscape is small molecules and peptides only.
critical_gaps: Target validity of the small-molecule TrkB agonists. Whether LM22A-4 / 7,8-DHF engage TrkB at brain-achievable free concentrations is unresolved; a challenge in the wider literature was flagged but could not be retrieved or verified, and 7,8-DHF pleiotropy is independently indicated (INFERENCE, PMID 36764626; PMID 28677406). This single unknown gates all TrkB chemistry investment.

Per-cell switch rate for Xi reactivation: what fraction of individual null neurons an ASO alone - without a DNMT inhibitor - can flip to wild-type MECP2 expression in vivo, by region including brainstem, and whether that is separable from chromosome-wide X reactivation (EVIDENCE basis, PMID 29282321).

Whether a per-cell therapeutic window exists in a mosaic brain for any MeCP2-adding agent. Nuclear MeCP2 occupancy has never been reported per cell or per cell type in Mecp2+/- females, so the dose window for protein and mRNA is formally undefined (INFERENCE, PMID 35460749; PMID 26605526).

The minimum corrected-cell fraction needed for clinical benefit in a mosaic brain; unquantified as a design parameter, and it determines whether any cell-fraction-limited modality can work at all (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

Whether the apnoea endpoint is measurable with enough state-resolved signal-to-noise to detect a true drug effect, and why sarizotan failed - wrong node, no brainstem engagement, or endpoint failure (EVIDENCE, NCT02790034; INFERENCE, PMID 25147297).
Brainstem exposure of intranasal neurotrophins in a human-sized brain, where nose-to-brainstem distance is ~10 cm versus ~1-2 cm in mouse (INFERENCE, PMID 37633263).

Mouse-to-human intrathecal biodistribution scaling for deep structures and brainstem - the largest shared extrapolation gap for every CSF-delivered modality here (INFERENCE from nusinersen/tofersen precedent; PMID 26605526).
Size of the MECP2 splice-site / pseudoexon stratum, which determines whether a conventional, clinically precedented splice-switching ASO is worth any effort (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

next_actions.action: Blinded orthogonal TrkB target deconvolution for LM22A-4 and 7,8-DHF: full pTrkB concentration-response against a recombinant BDNF reference in TrkB reporter cells and primary Mecp2-null cortical neurons; repeat in TrkB-knockdown/knockout neurons; ANA-12 and K-252a epistasis at matched exposures; free brain concentration at the in vivo efficacious dose versus in vitro EC50; chemoproteomics if phenotype survives TrkB loss.
next_actions.question_answered: Are the reported small-molecule TrkB agonists genuine TrkB agonists at brain-achievable exposures, or is the published Mecp2 rescue off-target pharmacology?
next_actions.activity_required: Cell and primary-neuron pharmacology with a quantitative pTrkB assay plus free-brain-concentration PK; no new model construction. Must be blinded and powered with a BDNF reference curve and a TrkB-null negative control, since phospho-TrkB tissue westerns are the historic source of irreproducibility.
next_actions.supports_if: Reproducible, TrkB-dependent, ANA-12-shiftable pTrkB activation with free brain exposure above EC50. The target is pharmacologically valid: invest in TrkB partial-agonist chemistry with pTrkB as the dose-selection biomarker and build the pivotal animal study on brainstem apnoea.
next_actions.kills_if: No concentration-dependent pTrkB signal, or effects preserved in TrkB-knockdown neurons, or free brain exposure far below EC50. Stop all TrkB chemistry; redirect to chemoproteomic identification of the real mediator and to the IGF-1 branch. Do not progress a compound whose SAR would track an unknown off-target.

next_actions.action: Brainstem endpoint-qualification plus engagement-anchored pharmacology in symptomatic Mecp2+/- females. Arm A (drug-free): three repeated plethysmography + EEG/EMG sessions per animal to compute within-animal test-retest variance and detectable effect size for state-stratified versus total apnoea rate. Arm B (within-animal crossover): LM22A-4 and fenfluramine dosed to pre-declared exposures, with sarizotan as a built-in human-negative benchmark; terminal nTS slice recordings in the same animals as an independent engagement measure. Pre-register state-stratified apnoea rate as primary.
next_actions.question_answered: Is the apnoea endpoint measurable with enough state-resolved signal-to-noise to detect a true effect, and does any agent produce verified nTS engagement at a dose that reduces apnoea within an arousal state? That is: why did sarizotan fail?
next_actions.activity_required: In vivo plethysmography with arousal-state scoring plus terminal brainstem slice electrophysiology in an existing model. Should be resourced jointly with action 1 around LM22A-4 rather than funded twice.
next_actions.supports_if: State stratification materially lowers variance and detects an LM22A-4 apnoea reduction accompanied by normalised nTS synaptic drive, while sarizotan shows little nTS engagement at tolerated exposure. Sarizotan then failed for node/engagement reasons: advance the engagement-validated branch and fund human state-resolved polysomnography endpoint development first.
next_actions.kills_if: Variance stays high even after state stratification (no feasible trial could detect a plausible effect - spend on endpoint development, not molecules); or nTS drive normalises with apnoea unchanged; or apnoea reduction tracks arousal/activity rather than engagement. Any of these deprioritises brainstem E/I stabilisation as a standalone strategy.

next_actions.action: Cell-resolution ASO-alone dose-ranging for Xi reactivation: dose symptomatic allele-distinguishable Mecp2+/- females ICV with a Xist RNase-H ASO across 3-4 doses, with ASO-alone arms, a short-course 5-aza-dC positive control to anchor the achievable ceiling, and scramble controls. At 2 and 6 weeks microdissect cortex, hippocampus and brainstem for Xist RT-qPCR, allele-specific single-nucleus RNA-seq scoring per-neuron wild-type MECP2 expression, the number of co-reactivated X-linked genes in the same cells, and MeCP2 immunostaining. Parallel human arm: patient iPSC neurons with human XIST ASOs scoring allelic MECP2 and H3K9/H4K16 acetylation reversal.
next_actions.question_answered: Can an ASO alone, without a DNA-methyltransferase inhibitor, flip a large fraction of individual MeCP2-null neurons to wild-type MECP2 expression in vivo at tolerable doses - and without chromosome-wide X reactivation?
next_actions.activity_required: In vivo ASO dosing with allele-specific single-nucleus sequencing and regional mapping; parallel patient iPSC neuron pharmacology. Primary endpoint must be percent of neurons converted per region, explicitly not any behavioural measure.
next_actions.supports_if: ASO alone converts a substantial fraction (pre-specify >=25-30%) of null neurons in cortex and hippocampus with measurable brainstem conversion, nuclear MeCP2 protein restored, and reactivation confined to few X-linked loci. The drug-like version exists: advance to human XIST ASO screening and brainstem-weighted delivery optimisation before any efficacy work.
next_actions.kills_if: Strong Xist knockdown but only a few percent conversion, or conversion only in superficial cortex with none in brainstem, or conversion inseparable from chromosome-wide X reactivation, or conversion requires the DNMT inhibitor. Stop the Xi-reactivation ASO programme as a standalone therapeutic; DNMT dependence converts it into an epigenetic-reprogramming safety problem and should be deprioritised rather than reformulated.

next_actions.action: Desk analysis, days not months: enumerate the fraction of MECP2 patients carrying splice-site or pseudoexon-creating variants from curated variant databases, and separately check whether an independent published pharmacological challenge to LM22A-4/7,8-DHF TrkB agonism exists.
next_actions.question_answered: Is the splice-amenable stratum large enough to justify a conventional, clinically precedented ASO programme - and has the TrkB target-validity question already been settled in the literature?
next_actions.activity_required: Variant database curation plus a targeted literature check. Near-zero cost and should precede action 1, since a published negative on TrkB agonism would change action 1's design or make it unnecessary.
next_actions.supports_if: A non-trivial splice-amenable stratum exists, justifying a splice-switching ASO assessed on its own terms with mature chemistry and intrinsic dose capping. If a credible published TrkB challenge exists, action 1 narrows to confirming free brain exposure versus EC50.
next_actions.kills_if: The splice-amenable stratum is negligible - drop that sub-route and concentrate oligonucleotide effort on Xi reactivation.

next_actions.action: Low-cost patient iPSC-neuron construct screen (not an in vivo programme): transfect candidate MECP2 mRNA designs including trimmed methyl-DNA-binding plus NCoR-interaction domains with destabilising UTRs/degrons, measuring per-cell MeCP2 against endogenous plus H3K9/H4K16 acetylation reversal.
next_actions.question_answered: Can per-cell MeCP2 output from an exogenous transcript be capped near physiological at all, or is uncontrolled burst expression intrinsic to the modality?
next_actions.activity_required: In vitro human neuron transfection with quantitative per-cell MeCP2 immunofluorescence and the established acetylation potency assay. Months of bench time, no in vivo spend, no carrier development.
next_actions.supports_if: A design holds per-cell MeCP2 within roughly 1.5x endogenous while reversing H3K9/H4K16 hyperacetylation. Keeps the option alive for the day the field solves deep CNS neuronal mRNA delivery - but does not on its own justify a programme.
next_actions.kills_if: No design caps per-cell output. Closes MECP2 mRNA replacement permanently on pharmacology rather than on delivery, a cleaner and more durable answer.

do_not_fund_yet: Any MECP2 mRNA replacement programme. It would begin with CNS carrier invention rather than optimisation (EVIDENCE, PubMed zero hits for MECP2 mRNA/LNP; ClinicalTrials.gov Rett search), and mRNA's uncontrolled per-cell burst is the worst available match for a bidirectionally dose-sensitive chromatin reader (EVIDENCE, PMID 26605526). A generic CNS neuronal mRNA delivery screen is reusable across many indications and should not be charged to a Rett budget.

Human-sequence XIST ASO chemistry, brainstem delivery engineering or behavioural efficacy studies for Xi reactivation, before the per-cell conversion rate is measured with an ASO alone. Everything downstream is moot if the switch rate is low (EVIDENCE basis, PMID 29282321).

New TrkB agonist medicinal chemistry, dose selection or biomarker development before orthogonal quantitative pTrkB target validation. Committing SAR to a possibly mis-assigned mechanism is the dominant failure mode of this otherwise strongest approach (INFERENCE, PMID 36764626; PMID 28677406).

Another Rett respiratory-endpoint clinical trial using averaged, unstratified apnoea counts and dosed to a tolerability rather than target-engagement ceiling. That is precisely the design that produced the sarizotan null (EVIDENCE, NCT02790034; INFERENCE, PMID 25147297).

Protein engineering for cell-penetrating MeCP2 - BBB shuttles, humanised constructs, CMC - before per-cell nuclear occupancy curves in mutant- versus wild-type-expressing neurons of a mosaic female show that a window exists at all (INFERENCE, PMID 35460749; EVIDENCE, UniProt P51608).

Any efficacy study in this disease whose primary endpoint is rodent behaviour. Behavioural rescue occurs with persistent circuit abnormalities (EVIDENCE, PMID 40673967), so behaviour-primary studies will systematically overstate translatable benefit for every approach here.

A second-generation neurotrophin biologic positioned against approved trofinetide on a composite behavioural endpoint. Differentiation must be on respiratory/autonomic morbidity with demonstrated brainstem target engagement, or the programme has no viable clinical claim (INFERENCE, NCT04776746; PMID 37633263).
conclusion_note: The causal gene, mosaic architecture and post-onset reversibility are well established, so Rett can be responsibly planned - but no approach reviewed here earns PURSUE. The binding uncertainty is which downstream node to drug and within what dose window: the single most decision-relevant open item is whether the small-molecule TrkB agonists that generated the best brainstem and spine-density rescues are genuine TrkB agonists at all (INFERENCE, unverified), and the brainstem branch has one decisive human failure (NCT02790034) whose cause is unresolved. Three approaches are INVESTIGATE with cheap, well-specified killing experiments; MeCP2 protein is LOW PRIORITY because its non-selectivity in a mosaic tissue is structural rather than optimisable; MECP2 mRNA is REJECT on delivery and pharmacological mismatch. Decision support only, not medical advice.
